newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes steady, Brent cash spreads hold.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes steady, Brent cash spreads hold.

text.p: North Sea crudes were broadly steady in early Thursday talk as Brent cash spreads held firm, but spot markets were quiet with few unsold July cargoes and buyers reluctant in the face of deteriorating margins.
Aug Brent shed 12 cents to $18.80 a barrel on the IPE, erasing Wednesday's short-covering gains, but cash spreads were holding onto late U.S. levels.
"The paper market is firm but there's very little activity so far," said a trader.
Aug/Sep was talked either side of -3 cents, while Sep/Oct edged a couple of cents higher to -7/-4 cents, dealers said.

Brent Contacts for Difference (CFDs) were also little changed in early discussions with next week's dates (July 07-11) pegged at +5/+10 cents, holding a 10-15 cent backwardation over the following week.
With much of the July Brent programme nominated so far in the hands of one major, and most of the cargoes thought to be committed, talk on Dated Brent was thin.
Two July 18-20 cargoes were due to turn wet on Thursday.
Other North Sea grades were equally subdued with most of the prompt barrels placed and offers limited to late July cargoes, traders said.
"Most of the North Sea oil which has to be placed has gone and refiners are pretty well covered for the month," said a trader.
"What is being shown is late July barrels but it's a market without buyers. There's still a question mark hanging over Iraq's return so buyers prefer to do nothing," he added.
Others saw Ekofisk on offer at slightly lower numbers than last done but buyers were not biting, given sliding margins.
"There's a bit of Ekofisk around and the sellers may be prepared to come lower but buyers are hanging back because margins got whacked," said a trader.
